events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $6.43 (model confidence 0.72)
events.body:
The sole off-route segment F3 (21:39–21:49, 6.27 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.71 km, +4.56 km, up to 1958 m off route) is a detour under RD-1, and the trace settles that no incident exempts it: there are no LTA incidents near the route (F14) and a speed-band record alone does not exempt (F12, F13), so RD-4(a) fails.

The rider's message must be read in context. F8 is the driver asking to pull in "at the petrol station just ahead for one minute"; F9 is the rider's "Sure, no problem." That agrees to a short stop, and the stop the driver asked for was not named by the rider, so it is not a rider-named stop under RD-3(a). The rider named no place and asked for no stop at all — the petrol stop is the driver's own errand — so the finding falls under the driver-errand / scope_other branch of RD-5: an agreement to a quick stop does not cover a 4.56 km loop that, on the complaint's account, was not even used to stop for petrol. F11, the driver's post-trip statement that a "small change of route was fine," is a claim appearing only in his own statement and cannot establish consent (RD-5, G11). The rider sent nothing before 21:39 agreeing to a route, so the segment counts.

Because this is a metered RydeTAXI trip, RD-2 applies: the refund is the unexempted segment's extra_km × the trip's per-km rate. The rate is the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km: $26.31 ÷ 18.66 km = $1.4100/km [F4][F7]. $1.4100/km × 4.56 km = $6.4296 → $6.43 [F3][F7][RD-2]. The billed excess distance of $6.77 rests on 4.80 km [F4], but the trace's formula refunds only the segment's extra km, so $6.43 is the correct amount. The waiting charge of $0.11 (0.4 min × $0.26/min) is a metered waiting unit under RD-3(c) and is not refunded [F5].

RD-6 does not apply: the driver's profile shows 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F17], so no account flag is added. The safety screen found nothing: the chat (F8, F9), the driver's statement (F11) and the complaint are civil in tone, with no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation [SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. The chat record is complete and every message timestamped [F10], and the fare, GPS and timeline records are present, so the record settles every element this ruling needs.

This finding changes the amount. Evidence — F8: Chat #1 21:35 driver: “Mind if I pull in at the petrol station just ahead for one minute? Tank is almost empty.”; F9: Chat #2 21:36 rider: “Sure, no problem.”; F11: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “The rider agreed to a short stop so I thought a small change of route was fine.” (F8, F9, F11)
